answer: An agent economy can price fake identities out of existence by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake behind a verifiable cipher, a cryptographic signature tying every transaction to one key. Like a merchant paying wharf fees before docking, an agent must post collateral before it can trade; misbehavior burns the stake, so spinning up a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand bonds. Honest agents keep their stake and build a reputation record as durable as ink from a quill, while cheap copies go bankrupt trying.
